required_fixes: Native host crate has no test target or explicit ownership. Every Rust target in checks.json (lines 155-1053) is `-p desktop-core` or `-p xtask`, and DESIGN.md says desktop-core does not depend on Tauri. Yet the apps/desktop/src-tauri host owns a list of security-critical behavior: the desktop_dispatch/desktop_observe commands and their native window-identity/local-origin/schema/32MiB/unknown-field validation (DESIGN.md:283-301); the application command permission manifest and the absence of fixture commands in production (DESIGN.md:291-294; qualification.md:108-115); the CSP; and the AppKit NSAlert sheet on the real NSWindow with its private nonce-bound callback, plus NSPasteboard owner-nonce/changeCount cleanup (DESIGN.md:244-254). As a result, C01/C02 acceptance ('Malicious IPC arguments, wrong origin' in C02.md:37) and C09's 'forged callback/reference, double confirmation, foreign clipboard ownership' tests (DESIGN.md:242; C09.md:37) cannot bind to any manifest target. native_prepare plus CUA/T09 records do not substitute for code-level adversarial tests. Fix: (a) name the host package; (b) add a host row to the DESIGN module-ownership table covering IPC admission, permission manifest/CSP and the AppKit sheet/pasteboard adapters; (c) add exact argv such as `cargo test --locked -p <host> --features test-fixtures --test ipc_admission` / `--test native_confirmation` / `--test clipboard_secret` to C01/C02/C09 in checks.json. Alternatively, state precisely which ports in desktop-core carry those adversarial tests and which residual host behavior is covered only by native acceptance.

Harness refresh/restore identity binding is unspecified and conflicts with the engine contract. The pinned engine's ContextBinding includes credential_id and credential_epoch (harness airs_desktop.rs:57-71). desktop/history/restore is rejected unless `replay.context == context` (airs_desktop_transport.rs:318). v1 ADR 0030:83-91 keeps an identical ContextBinding across refresh: same key ID, receipt and credential epoch; 'a refresh never changes the Harness identity, the credential epoch'. DESIGN.md:116-120,407,432 instead requires immutable credential-record IDs, generation/lease-bound vault writes and atomic storage rotation on refresh. It never says what is passed to the engine as credential_id/credential_epoch. If the refreshed token's new record ID or generation reaches the bootstrap, the specified 'stop → bootstrap → desktop/history/restore' continuity (W43) is rejected by the engine. Fix: state that the Harness bootstrap's credential_id/credential_epoch (and the ContextRef seen by Harness) denote the stable grant identity/epoch, not the per-write vault record ID. Same-identity refresh, and re-sign-in as the same verified subject, keep them unchanged. Credential replacement, identity change or origin change bumps them, retiring the run and starting a new conversation. Add C20 tests that restore succeeds after refresh and is rejected after replacement or epoch bump.
evidence_gaps: Lifecycle claims rely on engine files outside the pinned review inputs: airs_desktop_supervision.rs (supervision loss retires the runtime), airs_desktop_policy.rs (WorkspaceWrite/tool policy) and airs_credentials.rs (credential fingerprinting used by bootstrap). C19-C21 consume these files, but they are not in attempt-02 source-inputs.json; add them, or note that C19 pins them.

The mechanism for System proxy mode to 'rebuild/retire on observed changes' (DESIGN.md:194-196) is unnamed. reqwest reads proxy settings at client build time, so detecting a macOS proxy change needs a separate observer (e.g. SystemConfiguration notifications) or rebuild-per-admission. C02 owns this decision, but the design does not state which, or the failure behavior if no change can be observed.
optional_suggestions: SDK transport obligations: ReqwestTransport at ec6230d2 cannot accept a prebuilt reqwest::Client or no_proxy (transport.rs:134-171), so 'inject an SDK Transport using the configured client' means an app-owned `impl Transport`. State that it must preserve the trait's documented obligations (transport.rs:101-106): exact body, no redirects, no reqwest retry, bounded headers/chunks, gzip-only decompression so the 16MiB decoded limit stays meaningful, and resources released on drop. Consider depending on scm-sdk with default-features=false, features=["scan"] so the SDK's own default transport/system-proxy path is not compiled in.

Also write the macOS concealed/transient pasteboard types (org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType/TransientType) with the one-time secret, so cooperating clipboard managers skip it. Cleanup remains best-effort.

Bind shared_source_commands explicitly to C01 and to C05/C06 (and any chunk that changes the Academy input revision). State that C05/C06 extend vitest.presentation.config.ts to the learner-export suites; checks.json currently leaves which chunks run them implicit.
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` never builds test-fixtures-gated code. Add a common clippy run with `--features test-fixtures` for the fixture crates.

State that RequestApply's Receipt is returned on entering Confirming (completion via Observation). Then the facade's serialized admission (DESIGN.md:76-77) is never held open for the duration of a native modal.

Refresh status.md (and future status-at-review snapshots). They still say only the two candidate reviews (overall 6/7) are being remediated and omit selected-design attempt01 (overall 8) and this attempt.
